title: The Fastest Bird
blurb: Which bird is the fastest on Earth? Finn and Zeb climb a church tower in the city to find out.
cover_prompt: Finn and Zeb stand on the top of an old stone church tower above a city, Zeb holding up his camera and Finn holding binoculars, as a peregrine falcon with a dark head and pale speckled chest dives past them like a dart through the blue sky.
outfits: , wearing a khaki explorer shirt and shorts and a green safari hat, with binoculars round his neck
, wearing the same khaki explorer outfit and green safari hat, with a camera on a strap round his neck

sound.label: /ur/
sound.intro: Listen for the /ur/ sound, as in bird. In this story it is spelt three ways. Tap a word to hear it.

cracked: The peregrine falcon is the fastest bird on Earth. Finn and Zeb cracked the case!

text: Finn and Zeb are in the Den. Ping!
Which bird is the fastest on Earth?
p1.prompt: Inside the cosy explorer den, the wall screen flashes with a picture of a bird shape zooming past with speed lines; Finn grabs his binoculars and Zeb grabs his camera, both excited.

text: A ranger sends a clue: a bird that nests
on a church in the city. Let's search!
p2.prompt: Finn and Zeb look at the den wall screen, which shows a friendly ranger in a green fleece standing in front of a tall old stone church tower in a city, pointing up at a nest on a ledge; Finn reads his map, Zeb jumps with excitement.

text: They get to the church first thing.
Its tower is as tall as ten houses!
p3.prompt: Early morning in a busy city: Finn and Zeb stand at the bottom of a huge old stone church tower with pointed windows and a tall spire, craning their necks to look all the way up; pigeons on the steps, red buses passing.

text: The ranger sets up a big telescope.
Look! A bird on the third ledge up.
p4.prompt: A friendly ranger in a green fleece sets up a big telescope on a tripod in a churchyard and Finn looks through it while Zeb points up at a small bird sitting on a high stone ledge of the church tower.

text: It has a dark head, like a helmet,
and a pale chest. It is a girl falcon.
p5.prompt: Close view, as if seen through a telescope, of a peregrine falcon perched on a stone ledge of a church tower: dark slate-grey head like a helmet, yellow around the eye and beak, pale chest with fine dark bars; a round telescope-view edge is NOT drawn, the picture fills the frame.

text: Do they go up the tower stairs, or
stay and watch from the church yard?
c1.prompt: At the foot of the old church tower, an open wooden door shows a spiral stone staircase going up, while a sunny churchyard with a bench and a telescope is on the other side; Finn points up the stairs, Zeb points at the bench.

text: Up they go, step after step. They burst
out at the top, puffing. What a sight!
b1a.prompt: Finn and Zeb burst out of a little door onto the top of the church tower, puffing and grinning, with the whole city spread out below them under a blue sky; the ranger follows behind.

text: They sit on a bench in the church yard.
Zeb spots a feather twirling down.
b1b.prompt: Finn and Zeb sit on a wooden bench in a sunny churchyard with the tall tower behind them; Zeb reaches up to catch a single grey feather twirling down through the air, Finn watches through binoculars.

text: Then she tips over and dives! She curls
her wings in, like a dart. Whoosh!
p6.prompt: A peregrine falcon dives headfirst down past the church tower with its wings tucked in tight like a dart, speed lines streaming behind it, against a bright blue sky; Finn and Zeb watch with mouths open.

text: She is faster than a car on a motorway.
No bird on Earth can dive faster!
p7.prompt: A fun picture-book comparison: the diving peregrine falcon zooms past a red car on a motorway far below and is clearly much faster, with long speed lines; Finn and Zeb cheer from the tower top.

text: A flock of birds scatters. Swirl!
She misses, and turns back up. Whew!
p8.prompt: A flock of grey pigeons scatters in a swirl over the city rooftops, all of them safe, while the peregrine falcon swoops past them and curves back up into the sky; Zeb laughs with relief, Finn points.

text: She lands back on her ledge. Chirp, chirp!
Three fluffy chicks peep out of the nest.
p9.prompt: On a high stone ledge of the church tower, the peregrine falcon lands beside a nest with three fluffy white chicks with big dark eyes, beaks open, peeping; seen from close by, a sunny city behind.

text: The church wants a camera on the nest so
people can watch. What do you think?

reveal.text: Lots of cathedrals do put cameras by falcon nests, so people all over can watch the chicks grow. Others say: give the birds peace, and watch from far away with a telescope. By law, nobody may disturb a falcon nest. What do you think?

c2.prompt: In the churchyard, the friendly ranger holds up a small nest camera while Finn and Zeb look up at the high ledge where the falcon family sits; Finn rubs his chin thinking, Zeb looks from the camera to the nest.

text: A small camera goes up by the nest.
Now people all over can see the birds!
b2a.prompt: A screen in the church shows a live picture of the three fluffy falcon chicks from a small camera on the ledge, and a happy crowd of children and grown-ups gathers round to watch; Finn and Zeb at the front, smiling.

text: They leave the birds in peace.
The chicks curl up and snooze.
b2b.prompt: Up on the quiet ledge, three fluffy white falcon chicks curl up together and snooze under their mother's wing; far below in the churchyard Finn and Zeb walk away quietly on tiptoe, smiling.

text: They watch from far with the telescope.
Zeb sees the first chick flap its wings!
b2c.prompt: Zeb looks through the big telescope on its tripod in the churchyard, gasping with delight; an inset of the view shows the first fluffy falcon chick flapping its little wings on the high ledge; Finn gives a thumbs up.

text: Finn writes in his notebook: fastest
bird on Earth, nests on churches.
p10.prompt: Finn sits on the churchyard wall writing in his notebook, which shows a simple drawing of a diving falcon and a church tower with a tick; Zeb sits beside him looking at the photos on his camera.

text: The sun sets. Get the train home first,
or stay to see her last flight?
c3.prompt: Sunset over the city, the church tower glowing orange; on one side the lights of a train station, on the other the falcon perched on the tower ready to fly; Finn looks at his watch, Zeb points up at the falcon.

text: On the train, Zeb curls up and snores.
Finn draws the falcon diving. Whoosh!
b3a.prompt: Inside a cosy train carriage at dusk, Zeb is curled up asleep on the seat with his camera, while Finn draws a diving falcon in his notebook; city lights pass by the window.

text: She swirls up high, then turns and dives
one last time, a dark dart in the sky.
b3b.prompt: At sunset the peregrine falcon swirls high above the glowing church tower and then dives like a dark dart across an orange and pink sky; Finn and Zeb watch from the churchyard, silhouetted, arms up in delight.

text: Back in the Den, Finn pins up the bird.
Fastest on Earth! Case cracked!
p11.prompt: Back in the cosy explorer den, Finn pins a drawing of a diving peregrine falcon onto the corkboard of case notes while Zeb holds out his arms like wings, pretending to dive; the wall screen shows a big green tick.

casefile.title: Peregrine falcon
casefile.subtitle: The fastest bird on Earth.

facts.text: A peregrine can dive at 320 km an hour. That is about three times as fast as a car on a motorway.
Peregrines nest on sea cliffs. Now some nest on tall buildings in towns, like cathedrals.
In 1961 there were only 385 pairs in the UK. Now there are lots more!

casefile.prompt: A Creature Cases style fact file portrait of a peregrine falcon perched proudly on a stone ledge, dark slate-grey head like a helmet, yellow eye-ring and feet, pale chest with fine bars, wings slightly open, with a sea cliff and a church tower in the background; clean, bright, centred, like a collector card illustration, no people.

quiz.q: Which picture shows the falcon diving?
quiz.why: Wings curled in, like a dart.
On a ledge, high up on the church.

quiz.q: Why did she curl her wings in when she dived?

options.text: To go faster, like a dart

quiz.q: Why do people keep away from a falcon nest?

options.text: So the birds are not upset
Because falcons do not like chips

quiz.why: The birds need peace to look after their chicks.

debrief.question: Would you put a camera on the nest? Why?
